course.name: Storage and Tables
course.description: Import a small dataset, update it safely and verify persisted results.
course.longDescription: 35 minutes required. Prerequisite: Thinking in Flows. Use supplied synthetic rows to practice storage scope, stable identities, upserts and write verification. Optional SQL and ontology classes take 12 minutes each. Retrieval and source evaluation now belong to the separate RAG course.

modules.title: Build and check
modules.description: Complete the practical steps and inspect the result.

challenges.prompt: A status changes on ticket T-002. Which identity should an upsert use?

options.label: The existing ticket_id T-002.
A new random ID for every import attempt.
Only the timestamp of the latest run.

challenges.prompt: A retry sees the same filename but a different content hash. What does that establish?
challenges.explanation: The contents changed; treat it as a new source version and reconcile by stable record IDs.

options.label: The prior import must be ignored because filenames are authoritative IDs.
The file is necessarily malicious.
The contents changed; treat it as a new source version and reconcile by stable record IDs.

lessons.title: Upsert three records and run twice

challenges.prompt: The second run creates six rows after a three-row first run. Which design should you inspect first?
challenges.explanation: Whether writes use stable ticket_id values and Batch Upsert with the correct ID Column.

options.label: Whether the app banner is cached.
Whether writes use stable ticket_id values and Batch Upsert with the correct ID Column.
Whether the table name is long enough.

challenges.prompt: A join doubles every ticket for one customer. Which check comes first?
challenges.explanation: Check whether the customer source has multiple matching rows per customer_id.

options.label: Check whether the customer source has multiple matching rows per customer_id.

challenges.explanation: The overlay mappings and dependent queries/actions that reference that column.

options.label: A nightly duplicate table containing all graph rows.
The ontology color palette.

lessons.title: Import a new ticket and explain the result

challenges.prompt: A retry must update the same ticket even after its file is renamed. Which key should persist?
challenges.explanation: The source business ticket_id, with file identity kept separately as provenance.

options.label: A new random key on every run.
The source business ticket_id, with file identity kept separately as provenance.
The new filename plus the current time.

challenges.prompt: A write takes its Error output but a later branch prints Import complete. What must change?
challenges.explanation: Stop or report failure on the error branch; confirm all required writes before reporting completion.

options.label: Stop or report failure on the error branch; confirm all required writes before reporting completion.
Rename the success message to make it clearer.
Run Count against any unrelated table.

challenges.prompt: The import count is correct. What additional evidence proves the changed fixture applied?
challenges.explanation: Inspect T-002 and confirm its status is closed.

options.label: Only inspect the run duration.
Check whether the app route is unique.
Inspect T-002 and confirm its status is closed.
